lead_headline: Restaurant tracker emerges from 18-day freeze with zero new leads for Saturday—foreclosure docket empties above $4M

restaurant.blurb: Zero new leads today—tracker extends June shutdown to 19 consecutive days as Saturday detection infrastructure remains frozen across metro neighborhoods.

liquor.blurb: 350 new applications today—Saturday surge breaks two-week freeze with massive licensing dump. Denver issuing approvals for Spitz Mediterranean (2615 Walnut), Dry Dock Pub on Pearl (1101 S Pearl), Madeline (1313 E 6th Ave), and Noble Steakhouse (1525 Blake). Hotel & Restaurant licenses dominate new filings, with RiNo, Capitol Hill, and LoDo neighborhoods leading approvals. Tobacco retailer permits jumped citywide, QuikTrip and 7-Eleven expanding convenience store footprint. Associated Person permits flooded docket as ownership shuffles accelerate across metro. No status changes or removals logged—system processing backlog from June's two-week dormancy.

reputation.blurb: 5 mentions yesterday—Friday coverage surged from Thursday's zero with Denver Post Lakewood office tower sale and Lucky Bastard Saloon closure leading pickups. Weekly tally: 47 mentions across 11 sources, up 15% from prior week's 41 as mid-June momentum recovers sharply. Denver Post dominated with 19 citations (40% share), Reddit contributed 7, Facebook/X/Instagram each logged 4. Notable week: Lakewood's tallest office tower sold at 30% discount, Lucky Bastard finally closed after two years on market. Week-over-week gain reverses May's slide as media attention rebuilds entering weekend, Google News RSS driving 96% of discovery with Reddit RSS accounting for remaining 4%.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 yesterday (3 new, 0 canceled) lifts MTD net to +13 (+1.1/day), 90-day net now at +130. Friday's clean gain breaks Thursday's flat pattern as weekend approaches. Recent fortnight shows mixed signals: five zero-net days scattered among modest gains, with June 5's +4 spike and yesterday's +3 providing only meaningful upward pressure. Current 7-day window (+5) trails prior period (+9) by 44% as June's daily pace (+1.1) remains stubbornly below YTD velocity (+1.2), confirming persistent cooling from Q1's stronger run despite Friday's improvement.
